audit_result.proof_trace: reduce_outflow always modifies the segment at the caller's current timestamp (now/segment_duration), not the segment where the original add_outflow was recorded. When a deposit occurs in a different time segment than the preceding withdrawal, reduce_outflow resets the current segment to 0 (line 110-112) then finds 0 <= reduced_value and leaves it at 0 — so the original withdrawal segment is never decremented. The NOTE at line 98-99 implicitly acknowledges this: 'reducing a HUGE number of outflow of current segment doesn't affect the total value of outflow in a cycle' when the outflow sits in another segment.
audit_result.attack_scenario: User withdraws 900 tokens at time T1 (add_outflow records in segment S1); user then deposits 900 tokens at time T2 > T1+segment_duration (reduce_outflow operates on empty segment S2, leaving S1 unchanged at 900); the rate limiter still reports 900 net outflow despite the full re-deposit, preventing any further withdrawals until S1 naturally expires after the full cycle duration.

PROP-01b-partial2-inv-040.text: Rate limiter deposit reduce_outflow on deposit must correctly offset prior add_outflow on withdraw.
PROP-01b-partial2-inv-040.assertion: deposit: emode.deposit_limiter.reduce_outflow(now, amount) reduces current segment value
